newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot products pounded in NYMEX selloff.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot products pounded in NYMEX selloff.

text.p: U.S. spot products prices were pounded with NYMEX futures late Thursday, with Gulf M4-grade conventional unleaded gasoline tumbling six cents a gallon as it forfeited all of yesterday's 2.50 cent differentials gain, traders said.

All eyes were glued to the NYMEX screen as products prices steadily fell, with November gasoline losing 3.44 cents a gallon and November heat sliding 2.12 cents by the end of the session and the expiry of November futures contracts.

Gulf M4-grade found itself in double trouble as major refiners -- whose brisk buying firmed diffs 2.5 cents a gallon on Wednesday, vanished. By midafternoon offers fell to a half cent over December futures from their starting point of 3.0 cents over.
Traders said majors bought heartily Wednesday, spurred in part by an approaching deadline for shipping front-31st cycle M4 on the Colonial Pipeline and a spate of refinery problems.
But some expressed confusion at the extent of today's NYMEX volatility, noting gasoline futures had jumped sharply on Wednesday.
